verdicts.evidence: repro/A9-verify/a9-01-shutdown-waits-pacer.ts (node 24, real startLoop + RedditPacer, gap scaled to 2 s): output in a9-01.out = 'claim#1 at 0ms / stop() at 501ms / claim#2 at 2001ms / stopped resolved at 2001ms / REPRODUCED'. runner.ts:67-70 stop() only wakes the loop's own sleep; pacing.ts:48-55 acquire() uses its own non-interruptible sleepFn; poll.ts:36-38 claims right after acquire returns; index.ts:315 awaits every loop before releaseAllClaims/deregister. REDDIT_MAX_RPM defaults to 1 (config.ts:63) and deploy-workers.sh never sets it, so the gap is 60 s and trace.ts:86 shares the same pacer; docker stop -t 35 (deploy-workers.sh:63). watch.ts:77-82 pages 'Reddit worker down' for a row silent >= 600 s (heartbeat.ts:16) and nothing prunes rows automatically.
verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real: shutdown waits out the pacer and can even take a fresh claim after SIGTERM. 'Usually' overstates it, though. The poll loop sleeps 15 s idle (index.ts:244, interruptible), so acquire waits about 45 s, and SIGTERM only lands more than 35 s from the end for a minority of the cycle. Also, a SIGKILL during acquire holds no subreddit claim. The robust consequence is a stale workers row plus a false 'worker down' page, and the claims self-heal via TTL, with no data loss. Prod read-only snapshot: all 7 worker/api rows started 2026-10-31 09:00 UTC, 0 stale rows, 0 watch_alerts, so today's fleet-wide restart left no orphan rows. Operational noise, so P3.

verdicts.evidence: repro/A9-verify/a9-02-console-marks-notified.test.ts (vitest against own PG18 :55709, real migrations): a 'target' post with telegram_chat_ids=['buyer-chat'] goes through notifyOnce with createConsoleAlertSender, ends status='notified', and fetch is never called. PASS, a9-02.out. Cause: alerts.ts:63 returns delivered=[chatIds] for console, and notify.ts:85-88 marks notified. deploy-workers.sh:33 defaults ALERT_TRANSPORT to console, and secrets.env.example:19 sets ALERT_TRANSPORT=console explicitly. Mitigation found: notify.ts:48, workers with deferToUserSender skip notify entirely while the api's Telegram user session is live (<120 s). Prod read-only: telegram_state user sender live=t, the api service has TELEGRAM_USER_SESSION set, and for weeks 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-26, 145/145 notified posts have alert_messages rows (real sends). Railway worker ALERT_TRANSPORT=telegram.
verdicts.reason: The code path reproduces exactly. In prod, workers only notify when the api's user sender is down or released (api redeploy/session loss), so the leak is limited to those windows and needs a VM misconfigured to console. Whether any OCI VM actually runs console could not be checked: there is no terraform state/IPs here, and the .env holds secrets. It is a latent footgun with a default that points the wrong way, not an observed loss. P3 unless the owner finds a console VM, in which case it is P2.

verdicts.evidence: Premise confirmed: Railway worker service eed8d23f-0462-4a84-8a2e-14edf0a880de has WORKER_ID=railway-worker (railway variables, value non-secret). Not reachable today: the service has no drainingSeconds/overlapSeconds (railway status --json: both null; get-service-config shows none; no RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS / _OVERLAP_SECONDS in the variable names; railway.toml has no teardown settings). Railway docs (docs.railway.com/variables/reference): 'RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS: The SIGTERM to SIGKILL buffer time, its default value is 0'. The old deployment is SIGKILLed at once, so index.ts:315-325 (await loops, which includes a pacer wait of up to 60 s, then releaseAllClaims/deregister) never runs. The old process can't release the new one's claims or lease or delete its row.
verdicts.reason: The harmful path needs the old process to finish its shutdown while the new one is running, and with Railway's 0 s default drain it never gets there. The fixed id actually makes Railway immune to A9-01's orphan row, because the new process upserts the same row. This is a latent trap only: if someone sets a draining period of 40 s or more (e.g. as the fix for A9-01), it becomes real. In that case, use a per-process id or have shutdown release only rows it claimed (claimed_at > its own start). P3 note, not P2.
